title: Aurora Mobile MoonFox Data | Salomon’s Rise, Amer Sports Enters a Period of Robust Earnings
author: Moonfox Data
description: Amer Sports achieved $6.566 billion in annual revenue for 2025, up 26.7% year-on-year, with net profit surging 488.7% to $427 million. The company's DTC-driven strategy and expansion in Greater China and Asia-Pacific markets drove growth across all three core segments: technical apparel (Arc'teryx), outdoor performance (Salomon), and ball sports. The company plans continued store expansion in 2026 to capitalize on growing global outdoor sports demand.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong financial performance with 26.7% revenue growth, 488.7% net profit increase, improved gross margins (57.6%), and successful expansion of DTC channels and geographic markets. All three business segments achieved double-digit growth, and the company has clear growth strategies for 2026 with planned store expansions.

title: Apparel Earnings Winners and Losers: Ralph Lauren Takes Off
author: Leo Miller
description: Major apparel companies reported earnings with mixed stock market reactions despite all beating on sales and EPS. Ralph Lauren surged 13.9% on strong revenue growth of 17% YOY and EPS beat, with women's apparel and handbags performing particularly well. Amer Sports rose over 5% with 32% sales growth and raised full-year guidance significantly. Deckers Outdoor saw modest 1% gains despite strong results, with its Hoka brand reaching record quarterly revenue.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock surged 13.9% following strong fiscal Q4 2026 results with revenue up 17% YOY beating estimates by $130M, adjusted EPS up 23% YOY to $2.80 vs. $2.52 estimate, and solid FY2027 guidance of 4-5% sales growth with 40-60 basis points margin expansion.

Stock up over 5% post-earnings with 32% YOY sales growth to $1.95B (beat $1.84B estimate) and adjusted EPS up 40% YOY to $0.38 vs. $0.31 estimate. Company significantly raised full-year guidance to 20-22% sales growth and $1.18-$1.23 EPS, implying 24% EPS growth at midpoint.

Despite modest 1% opening gain, results were strong with 10% YOY revenue growth to $1.12B (beat by $30M+), adjusted EPS decline of only 4% YOY vs. anticipated 14% decline, Hoka brand at record $671M quarterly revenue, and strong FY2027 guidance plus $3.5B buyback authorization increase.

title: Amer Sports Stock Falls On Cautious Outlook
author: Lekha Gupta
description: Amer Sports stock fell 4.42% Tuesday despite beating Q4 earnings expectations (31 cents EPS vs. 28 cents consensus) and delivering 28% revenue growth to $2.101 billion. The decline was driven by cautious forward guidance, with full-year 2026 EPS forecast of $1.10-$1.15 below the $1.15 consensus estimate, and Q1 2026 EPS guidance of 28-30 cents below the 32-cent estimate. However, full-year sales guidance of $7.617-$7.748 billion exceeded analyst expectations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock declined 4.42% due to below-consensus EPS guidance for both full-year 2026 ($1.10-$1.15 vs. $1.15 consensus) and Q1 2026 (28-30 cents vs. 32 cents consensus), despite beating Q4 results and delivering strong revenue growth. The cautious near-term outlook outweighed positive quarterly performance.

title: Why Amer Sports Stock Soared Today
author: Howard Smith
description: Amer Sports reported a strong Q3 with 30% revenue growth, boosted guidance for 2025, and saw stock price increase by over 9% due to strong performance in Salomon footwear and Arc'teryx brands.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company exceeded sales expectations, raised guidance for 2025, showed strong revenue growth of 30%, and demonstrated resilience in challenging global trade environment
